title: Lorwyn Eclipsed Commander: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: Harrowed but still harrowing.
Ajani's heart went out to those changed by the aurora's tides. Having selfhood ripped away was still a painfully familiar feeling.
"Come into the light, strange one. All are welcome to bask in Eirdu's glow." —Kithkin rite-leader
"I told you not to build it with blighted wood." —Lysh, kithkin wickersmith
A forest that never thirsts always flourishes.
Shadowmoor is rife with wild magic—powerful but as volatile as the plane itself.
It is accompanied by the agonized squeals of faeries caught in its sap.
Lorwyn contains many such places: not bustling, not frenetic, but teeming with life in their own, quiet way.
In far-off Shadowmoor, her kin lifted their heads to a refrain they could not hear.
Blowflies only infest corpses, but if none are available, they have no trouble making some.
No one asked the springjack what it wanted.
A swarm ever grows in its wake.
A haunted husk of bark, its cursed whispers linger on the wind.
"You, toadlet! Bring me a goblet of your bog's finest fire-slug slime!"
Faeries trade trinkets for tales, growing their knowledge and his collection.
"No matter our differences, one thing we agree on: It ends in fire."
Eirdu's adherents invoke its blessings with jingling bells and dancing feet. Where there is joy, there is the warmth of the sun.
Isilu's adherents invoke its blessings with contemplation at sites marked by standing stones. Where there is quiet, there is the moon's inspiration.
"Meadowlarks sing in sun-touched skies And breezes kiss where Eirdu lies." —Verselet of Lorwyn
"Wanderers creep 'neath dark moonrise And wildness seethes where Isilu lies." —Verselet of Shadowmoor
"The Path of Flame is a flamekin's most personal journey. You must walk it for yourself, but you'll never walk alone." —Zasharua, Brighthearth mentor
The boggarts' construction methods were chaotic and reckless, but the resulting tower became the envy of Rotbog warren.
Life is nothing more than decay postponed.
Shadowmoor contains many such places: not evil, not malevolent, but pulsing with something bitter and eldritch.
When the gods go to war, mortals pay the highest price.
"Under the suns, Mirrodin kneels and begs us for perfection." —Geth, Lord of the Vault
Every contagion has a host.
They spawn from shadow, wreaking chaos until shadow claims them again.
Death in form and function.
Shadowmoor's main crops are rot, slime, and despair.
Ancient evils dwell within the burning chasm called the Ashmouth, ever ready to devour those foolish enough to travel alone.
"'Did I do it?' You'll have to be more specific."
Many have heard the beginning of its low, sustained shriek but few the end.
"I have seen things that would reduce a weaker person to blubbering and raving. Want to hear about them?" —Vraska
As the Eldrazi spread, no secret that could give Zendikar's defenders an advantage was considered too dangerous to seek.
In the tight-knit doun of Mistmeadow, death is less important than duty.
"Your creations are effective, Sheoldred, but we must unite the flesh, not merely flay it." —Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
They once sought to unite with the flame of transcendence. Now they seek only to extinguish the lights of others.
"Holy places are no longer sanctuary from death, and death is no longer sanctuary from anything." —Thalia, Knight-Cathar
"Leave behind the sorrow of this body. Be blessed, being of light."
The soldier had given up his wealth, his title, even his home, but he had no room for regret. At last, he had saved his friend.
"We train for the improbable, like lightning striking the same place twice, or striking everywhere at once." —Nundari, Sea Gate militia captain
Elementals are ideas given form. This one is the idea of "smashitude."
"Be silent and listen to your inner fire. Only then can you walk the Path of Flame."
It sees shaped stone and carved wood as mutilations.
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.
"Mana lurks in all things, even in the depths of one's own heart."
"To care for yourself, cultivate the world. To care for the world, cultivate yourself."
The true strength of nature is not the raging storm or the charging rhino, but the inexorable vitality of life.
Many horrors take the bait of brave elf volunteers walking alone, only to fall to the blades of rescuers lurking nearby.
The castle finally got vengeance for enduring years of royally bad taste.
"Animals commune with their environment without the need for language. Theirs is a fundamental connection that surpasses flimsy words." —Vivien Reid
"The land grows only where the kami will it." —Dosan the Falling Leaf
"The curse is broken."
"Living scarecrows make a mockery of the natural order. Dead ones make fine hats."
"Not just any floriculturist can grow this caliber of nightbloom. We're looking for a rooftop hothouse with quite particular conditions." —Dr. A of the Foundway Associates
When night fell, the plane itself was scarred.
Her subtle smile is suffused with venom.
Even the oldest treefolk was but an acorn when Lorwyn's first mysteries were born.
Mounted cinders circle the blasted peak at Kulrath, hunting the Extinguisher.
"My child grew from rot and ruin, yet she bloomed." —Multani
"We are all decaying, always in a state of near-death. One moment without breath and we begin to break down." —Cevraya, Golgari shaman
"No, not 'washed' ashore. It *walked* ashore." —Shafring Hulm, beachcomber
"I've seen death before. My mother succumbing to illness, my comrades bleeding on the battlefield . . . But I'd never seen anything as dreadful as that." —Taani, berserker of Etlan
It is spring incarnate, its gentle warmth chasing away the last of winter's bite.
"Yarok grieves within the waste Of Bala Ged's corrupted land." —*Lament for Bala Ged*, stanza 1
By guild tradition, any puddle of multicolored light on the cobblestones can serve as neutral ground.
It harmonizes with the essence of its master.
"What do you have that I cannot obtain?" —Mairsil, the Pretender
Beware a scarecrow bearing gifts—especially sloshing vessels of acid.
Urza exploited nature to power his war machines; in time, nature exploited his war machines to renew itself.
Built in honor of Alara's creatures, the ziggurat vanished long ago. When Progenitus awakened, the temple emerged again.
On the volcanic continent of Akoum, bizarre vegetation clusters around gas vents, and jagged mountain peaks rise high into the air.
"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them." —Pulan, Bant orchardist
With a warm fire and a fresh catch, Temur hunters find respite in even the coldest climates.
On Naya, ambition and treachery are scarce, hunted nearly to extinction by the awe owed to terrestrial gods.
Dappled coats become armored hides. Soft jaws become razor tusks. Nestling play becomes the fight for survival.
"The people must know that the former seat of their oppression is cleansed. Throw open Qarsi's gates and let them see for themselves." —Kotis, the Fangkeeper
Along the outer girders, in gold filigree, are inscribed the names of all those who fell to their deaths during construction.
Cliffs echo and branches quake at the roar of life.
"The most important part of a stronghold isn't its armaments or its walls. It's the reason people have to defend it." —Gvar Barzeel, krumar captain
Jund is a world as cruel as those who call it home. Their brutal struggles scar the land even as it carves them in its image, a vicious circle spiraling out of control.
For wisdom's sake, it was built high to gaze on all things. For glory's sake, it was built high as a testament of power. For strength's sake, it was built high to repel all attacks.
The continent of Guul Draz is a geothermal swampland reeking of heat and decay.
The Conflux crashed together far-flung continents, like ships colliding in a storm.
As eons passed, the rock wore away, revealing the rich colors at the mountain's heart.
Far from human eyes, birds flit between vivid blossoms in a hidden paradise.
Wildflowers here bloom not with the season but with the ebb and flow of magic.
All the wonders of the natural world in one breathtaking microcosm.
Beauty appears in strange places for those with eyes to see it.
Farmers cut the trees and buried their dead. The dead rose up and killed the farmers. The trees grew back and strangled the dead.
